profile.behavior: A buoyant, agile aerialist that soars and catches mostly large insects on the wing, often eating in flight; it frequently hunts, roosts, and migrates in groups.
field_marks: Slender, small raptor with long, narrow, pointed wings
Pale gray head and underparts contrasting with a dark slate-gray back and upperwings
Black wingtips and a long, mostly square-tipped black tail
Red eye set in a blackish eye patch
Small, delicate, strongly hooked dark bill
Yellow to reddish-orange legs and feet
profile.habitat: Mature bottomland and riparian forest, open woodland and savanna, shelterbelts, parks, and other tree-lined areas adjoining open pasture, prairie, farmland, or water.

findings: The plate depicts an adult Mississippi Kite: the pale gray head and underparts, darker slate-gray upperparts, blackish eye patch, red iris, dark wingtips, and long black tail agree with the reference photographs and live identification sources.

The primary specimen has one head, one correctly formed beak, one tail, two convincingly attached legs with intact feet, and a complete pair of wings; the far-side wing is naturally occluded by the side-on perched pose.

Both depicted bills have small, delicate raptor proportions. In the supplementary head study, the upper mandible is visibly longer than the lower mandible, projects moderately beyond it, and terminates in a strong hook consistent with the primary head and clearest side-profile reference.
The detached wing and head are clearly supplementary studies rather than extra birds or anatomy attached to the primary specimen; both are coherent and species-appropriate.

All visible names, taxonomy, measurements, habitat, behavior, and field-mark text are legible and correctly transcribe the proposed profile. The sex-specific length and weight values and the 75–83 cm adult wingspan are directly supported by Animal Diversity Web.

The body-length diagram increases correctly from 34 cm at the bottom to 37 cm at the top, repeats the printed sex-specific range without contradiction, uses centimeters consistently, and is explicitly labeled “SCHEMATIC — NOT TO SCALE.”
The layout is balanced and readable, with useful supplementary wing, head, and palette studies and no overlapping or malformed elements.
No place name used as observation metadata, ZIP code, coordinates, map, or local-observation detail appears; “Mississippi” occurs only within the species’ established common name.
